lines: Easy, kid. You've been out cold since yesterday.
Name's Tobi. Old Tobi, the kids say, though there aren't many kids left.
My old sword's in the chest by the hut. Take it. My knees can't swing it anymore.
And don't drink from the puddles. The water here kills you slower than the Spoiled, but it kills you.
Clean water? Out of that wreck? Huh.
I used to know someone who could do that. I think. My head's full of holes.
If you find old photographs out there, bring them back. Faces help me remember.
A lab coat. Ink on her fingers. She's laughing at something I said...
Ines. Her name was Ines.
We worked together, at a place in the hills. Water and soil. She was the clever one.
The old recycling yard. I ran the night shift on the sorting line.
She'd come at dawn with two coffees and a list of everything we did wrong.
She was always right. It was very annoying.
The river. We swam there. Before.
She said: 'The river remembers everything we pour into it.' I laughed at her.
I'm not laughing now, kid.
Lena's farm. We drove compost out from the city every week.
Then the trucks stopped. Then everything stopped.
That's me. On the Sanctuary roof, a power cable in my hands.
It got hard. The money went, the people went. And I... went too.
I left her there alone. That's the hole in my head, kid. I dug it myself.
If you get to the Sanctuary... no. I'll tell her myself. I'm coming.
The sixth of December. I don't know why I remember that.
Yes I do. That was the day I met her. Ines. At a bus stop in the rain.
If she locked something away, she'd use that day. Zero, six, one, two.
Mind the green puddles. My boots learned the hard way.
The generator? Clear the Spoiled first. They hate the light, but they hate the noise more.
Mira's on the roof again. Kid thinks that radio will talk back one day.
You sort like you mean it. Good. The world needs people who mean it.
Hey! You're the one who slept in the hut. I'm Mira. I fix things.
Well. I fix most things. My radio needs a valve. The glass kind, with a glow.
The Battery Factory made them. If you find one, I'll let you listen first. Deal?
Listen! Voices! Someone by the river is ALIVE!
He calls himself Osei. He says the Last Drop is real, but it's 'not what we think'.
What does that even mean? Grown-ups are so annoying.
The lights! I can see the whole street from the roof!
Tobi cried a little. Don't tell him I told you.
I'm going to be an engineer. Like the voice on your recorder.
Bottle caps are money. Don't let anyone tell you different.
Do you think the Spoiled were people once? Tobi says don't think about it.
Kip at the Dump says he has more bottle caps than me. He's lying.
Don't come closer! ...You're not one of them. Sorry. Sorry.
Halden. I was the chemist here.
Everything you see leaking out there, I signed off on it. Every month. 'Within limits.'
The limits were set by people who never drank this water.
You got the generator running. Then maybe you're the one for this.
Years ago I built a burner to clear dried sludge from the tanks. The pickers call it a rune now.
Take it. Press 1 to breathe fire. Burn what poisons, never what lives.
So you read it. The orders came from far away. Cheaper, faster, someone else's river.
It doesn't make me innocent. It makes all of us a little guilty.
That's harder to live with. And easier to fix.
You have been digging. I can tell by the dirt.
Copper. Three pieces, if you find them. My lab's wiring is mostly hope.
Bring them and I'll rewire the lab lights, and make you something.
Copper! Real copper. The lab will have light by tonight.
Here: crystal cells. I charged them from the lab. They feed your runes.
Batteries are tiny chemistry sets. Treat them like it.
Fire cleans sludge. It also cleans you right off the map if you stand in it.
Gloves first, questions later.
There was an old photo pinned in the lab. Someone took it out to the yard. Sentimental fools.
Another stray. Sit. No, not there. That's Kip's chair.
I'm Nana Ru. This heap is my kingdom, and everything in it has a price.
Sort for me and we'll trade. Nothing is free. Nothing is worthless either.
A perfect pile! Not one battery in the wrong bin. My pickers can't do that.
Here. An old scattergun the kids fitted with a rune. Press 2 and it roars.
It throws the Spoiled back. Use it to buy yourself time to think.
The records say every bag here had an address. Every single one.
People thought 'away' was a place. Away is my kitchen.
Crystal. From the deep mine, in the Industry. Bring me two.
Kip's birthday is coming. A child should have one thing that shines and isn't rubbish.
Two crystals. You don't haggle. Bad trader. Good person.
Take this plate. A soldier's, from before. Kip will never know where the crystals came from.
Glass goes for recycling. Broken glass? General waste, unless you like bleeding.
Kip is fast. Faster than you. Don't take it personally.
A heap is just a library nobody bothered to sort.
Food scraps make soil. Soil makes food. The old world forgot the second half.
Race you to the east heap! First one to sort it all wins.
Ninety seconds. Starting... NOW! Go go go!

challenge.label: Race Kip
challenge.win_text: You sorted the east heap before Kip.
challenge.lose_text: Kip got there first. You can still sort it.

lines: You beat me. You actually beat me. Nobody beats me.
Fine. Take my lucky stash. And my second-best bottle cap.
HA! Too slow! Nana, I won!
...it's okay. You sort right, and that's harder. Here, a consolation snack.
You sorted the east heap without even racing me? Rude.
Here, I found this in it before you did. So technically I still win.
I've got 412 bottle caps. Mira has 380. I'm winning.
The big Spoiled smell like old batteries. Don't ask how I know.
Nana pretends she doesn't like you. She does. She gave you the good chair.
Easy now. I'm not Spoiled, just ugly.
Osei. I keep the raft. If you came from the Outpost, maybe you've heard my voice.
The little one with the radio? Tell her I said: keep listening.
Clean water, running. I never thought I'd see it again.
Ines used to say the Last Drop isn't a spring. It's a promise that needs keeping.
The river gave me this rune. It belongs to whoever gave the river back. Press 3.
She's not waiting for you at the end of the road, you know.
She left you instructions. That's harder. And better.
If you go back to the Outpost, tell Tobi the river still remembers the two of them swimming.
No. Don't tell him. Just... see if he smiles.
Boiling kills germs. It doesn't kill poison. Remember that.
The fields upstream used to feed three cities.
Rivers forgive slowly. But they do forgive.
Clear water isn't clean water. The worst poisons have no colour.
If you're here to tell me the soil will come back, save your breath.
I'm Lena. This was my family's farm for four generations. Now it grows dust and Husks.
My brother Jory still plants things. Every morning. Every morning they die.
You built a compost bin? Like the ones we had before the trucks stopped?
...Jory, come here. Look what they did.
A tomato. A real one. I'd forgotten the smell of the leaves.
Thank you. I mean it. Take the rail line east when you're ready; the power is there.
The seedlings need clean water. Not the river, not yet.
Two flasks of purified water. A workbench can make them: sand, charcoal, a jar.
Clean water. Look at them drink.
Jory wants you to have these. He packed them himself. Badly.
Husks rise from the poisoned rows. Fire is the only thing they're scared of.
Never put plastic in compost. You'd be amazed what people tried.
Jory doesn't talk. He doesn't need to. Watch his hands.
Jory looks at you, then at the ground, then digs his hand into a hidden heap behind the barn.
It's warm. It's compost. He's been making it for years, in secret, because Lena stopped believing.
He presses a handful of old seeds into your palm and nods at the broken bin by the house.
Jory kneels by the garden bed and pushes his fingers into the dark soil.
He doesn't say anything. He doesn't have to. He's grinning.
Jory shows you a worm. He's very proud of the worm.
Jory points at the sky, then at the windmill, then shrugs. It turns anyway.
Jory taps a sign he painted: GREENS + BROWNS + AIR + TIME.
Stop right there. This plant is mine. These generators are mine.
My people live on what I keep running. Not on what some wandering kid wants.
You hear that rumble? That's my Golem. Fifty tonnes of slag and scrap. Turn around.
You... beat it. Nobody beats it.
Fine. FINE. I built that thing out of everything we couldn't get rid of. Maybe that was the problem.
The grid's yours. Just... share the power down the line. My people need light too.
Forty percent of the old power and everything runs. All those years I burned fuel for nothing.
I thought keeping it was the same as protecting it. It isn't.
My people are cold. The furnaces want coal and the mine is crawling.
Four lumps. You dig, I'll owe you.
Four lumps. The furnace will hold a week. My people will sleep warm.
I don't say this. Thank you. Take the key I found in the barn crate; I've no use for farms.
Read the labels, kid. Flammable, corrosive, toxic. The barrels don't lie.
The Wraiths come out of the smog. Hit them when you can see them.
Unit-7 sweeps that floor every day. It's the cleanest floor in a dead world.
UNIT-7 MAINTENANCE. FLOOR CLEANLINESS: 98 PERCENT. STAFF PRESENT: 0.
QUERY: ARE YOU STAFF?
...ASSIGNING YOU THE ROLE OF STAFF. WELCOME TO YOUR SHIFT.
POWER RESTORED. EFFICIENCY RATING: EXCELLENT. COMMENDATION LOGGED.
UNIT-7 REQUESTS TRANSFER TO THE SANCTUARY. FLOORS THERE ARE PROBABLY VERY DIRTY.
STAFF MEMBER: YOUR COMBAT CERTIFICATION IS OVERDUE.
NEUTRALISE THREE HOSTILES IN SIXTY SECONDS. TIMER STARTS... NOW.

challenge.label: Unit-7 drill
challenge.lose_text: CERTIFICATION: PENDING. UNIT-7 BELIEVES IN YOU.

lines: CERTIFICATION PASSED. EFFICIENCY: ADMIRABLE.
UNIT-7 HAS PRINTED YOU A BADGE. IT SAYS 'STAFF'. WEAR IT WITH PRIDE.
CERTIFICATION PENDING. UNIT-7 HAS LOGGED THIS AS A LEARNING EXPERIENCE.
LEARNING EXPERIENCES ARE ALSO VALUABLE. HAVE A BANDAGE.
QUERY: Did the farmer find the padlock code? I logged it in my bunker. Entry 4,411.
I log everything. Nobody reads the logs. I log that too.
SWEEPING. SWEEPING. SWEEPING.
DID YOU KNOW: A SWITCHED-OFF MACHINE USES ZERO POWER. UNIT-7 FINDS THIS BEAUTIFUL.
ACID ON FLOOR. DO NOT LICK.
INTRUDER DETECTED. SANCTUARY POWER: 3 PERCENT. SENTINELS ACTIVE.
IF YOU ARE A FRIEND, BRING POWER TO THE ATRIUM CORE.
IF YOU ARE NOT A FRIEND, THE SENTINELS WILL EXPLAIN.
POWER RESTORED. WELCOME, CARETAKER. SENTINELS STANDING DOWN.
THE ARCHIVE AWAITS SIX FRAGMENTS. ONE FROM EACH PLACE YOU CROSSED.
DR. VARGA LEFT INSTRUCTIONS FOR WHOEVER CAME. SHE WAS VERY SPECIFIC.
SEED BANK TEMPERATURE: NOMINAL. 41,000 VARIETIES. WAITING.
DR. VARGA SANG TO THE SEEDS. THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW WHY.
ALL SYSTEMS NEED CARETAKERS. EVEN THIS ONE.
Took me a while. Bad knees, long road. But I'm here.
She was right about everything, kid. Annoyingly right. Always.
I'll keep the water running here. It's the job I walked away from. I'd like it back.
She used to sing to the seeds. Terrible voice. I miss it.
Don't look at me like that. Old men are allowed to cry in gardens.
The river carried me up as far as it could. Then I walked.
A place like this needs someone who knows water. I know a little.
Clean channels, living soil. She built it to be shared.
Keep listening. That's all anyone has to do.
I followed the power line! Tobi tried to stop me. He failed.
There's a transmitter on the roof! With it, the whole world could hear this place.
...if you want them to. It's your call.
I'm going to fix every radio in the valley.
Bottle caps don't work here. I asked.
